item.title: Welcome
item.description: This is the home page of the Mountain Echo newspaper, a free community paper servicing the Midlands and Southern Drakensberg of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.The paper focuses on local news and offerings to everyone in its target area. It is printed and distributed on a monthly basis. Breathless [P. Welch]

item.title: Distinguished Alumnus L. Villines Returns to NAC in Workforce Role - Mountain Echo
item.description: HARRISON – North Arkansas College has announced the selection of Lewis Villines as its new Vice President for Technical Education and Workforce Development, a role that will focus on serving local workforce needs while expanding training programs and strengthening partnerships with school districts and employers across the region and the state. Villines will begin his new position on April 6, 2026.

item.title: Marion County Cattlemen meeting - Mountain Echo
item.description: The first 2026 dinner meeting of the Marion County Cattlemen’s Association will be held Tuesday, March 31, at 6:30 in the Yellville-Summit cafeteria.

item.title: 3 Manson Family members Arrested on multiple charges - Mountain Echo
item.description: By Gregg L. Alexander, Marion County Sheriff Marion County Sheriff Gregg Alexander reports the arrest of Steven M. Manson (35 YOM), Steven L. Manson (56 YOM), and Dezerae S. Manson (19 YOF), all of Yellville, on charges of Rape, a Class “Y” Felony, Incest, a Class “C” Felony, Sexual Assault 2nd Degree, a Class “B” Felony, Conduct Constituting Conspiracy, a Class “A” Felony, Coercion, a Class “A” Misdemeanor, and being an Habitual Offender.

item.title: Questions Mount Over Tax Filings, Penalties, and Donor Secrecy - Mountain Echo
item.description: BULL SHOALS — The Mountain Echo identified new public records and recent statements by city officials have raised significant questions about Bull Shoals’ handling of federal and state payroll tax filings, late penalties, and the city’s refusal to identify a private donor who paid more than $4,300 in IRS penalties on the city’s behalf.

item.title: Summer@ASMSA applications open for free 2026 summer camps - Mountain Echo
item.description: HOT SPRINGS — The Arkansas School for Mathematics, Sciences, and the Arts is accepting applications for 2026 Summer@ASMSA camps.

item.title: NAC Enrollment Reaches Highest Level in a Decade - Mountain Echo
item.description: – Enrollment at North Arkansas College has climbed to its highest level in a decade, highlighting the growing demand for college courses and early college opportunities among high school students.

item.title: A Friendly Message from Your Marion County Tax Collector - Mountain Echo
item.description: We are pleased to announce that the 2025 (payable 2026) tax books are now open.

item.title: Celebrating Women’s Military Service - Mountain Echo
item.description: By Hollie Scoma, President Military Service Sisters was founded in Mountain Home, Arkansas, in 2017 to serve the over 20,000 female veterans living in Arkansas, many of whom live in the Baxter County area. The organization, created by and for women veterans, now has several chapters statewide and has developed a strong working relationship with the Arkansas Department of Veteran Affairs to share resources with women veterans more effectively.

item.title: Hot and Cold Air for Beau and Hagrid - Mountain Echo
item.description: Crazy Arkansas weather strikes again! We do not know whether to get ready for floating the river or building a snowman!
